title: Raw HTML and Rendered DOM Are Separate Evidence
seoTitle: Raw HTML vs Rendered DOM: Capture and Compare Evidence
subtitle: Separate what the server delivered from what the browser built.
seoDescription: Compare server HTML with browser-rendered DOM using saved artifacts, explicit completion conditions and field-level diffs to diagnose JavaScript SEO failures.

artwork.alt: A monochrome source-document field faces a reconstructed rendered architecture across a bright boundary.
artwork.label: Rendering evidence / source and reconstruction
artwork.caption: Transport markup and browser-rendered state remain separate observations joined by an explicit rendering boundary.

author: SULAYMAN BOWLES
thesis: Save source and DOM as separate observations, then record the browser conditions between them. Their difference supports a finding only when the captures and completion state are understood.

conclusion.title: Rerun the same rendering test
conclusion.content: Keep source, DOM, and the conditions that joined them. After a repair, repeat the same capture and completion contract. A successful local render demonstrates that tested path; it does not establish indexing or every downstream crawler’s behavior.

evidenceBoundary: A controlled browser run describes the tested environment at a recorded time. It does not reproduce every search crawler, user device, cache state, geography, consent choice, or personalization path, and a successful local render does not prove indexing.

sources.label: Google Crawling Infrastructure: HTTP status codes

content: A server response and a rendered page can disagree in either direction. JavaScript may add content absent from the HTML or remove content the server delivered. Parsing, scripts, network activity, and mutations create the DOM. It and the raw response therefore answer different questions; neither alone explains the transformation.

Capture both artifacts with request metadata, browser identity, navigation timings, dependent-request outcomes, console errors, stop conditions, and completeness. That record lets a reviewer distinguish a page defect from a blocked resource, consent branch, timeout, authentication boundary, or failed instrument.

sections.title: Save what the server returned
paragraphs: Store the direct request target, headers, redirect chain, status, response headers, body hash, size, and timings together. Keep requested and final URLs distinct. A 200 application shell and a 200 response containing the article share a status, not a content outcome.

Keep response bytes alongside extracted fields. A later parser may need to distinguish an absent title, canonical, link, or structured record from an extraction miss. Record content encoding and character decoding too: replacement characters from a bad decode can resemble source defects.

Redirects, cache headers, content type, robots directives, and transport failures precede client execution. A screenshot cannot reconstruct a missing redirect hop or establish which markup the origin returned.

sections.title: Record the browser conditions
paragraphs: DOM output depends on engine and version, viewport, locale, time zone, cookies, storage, user agent, JavaScript policy, service workers, interception, authentication, and consent. Without those inputs, disagreeing runs cannot be compared. “Desktop render” is not enough.

Isolate contexts unless the test deliberately models a continuing session. Cookies can personalize a public route, service workers can return stale origin content, and shared storage can suppress a modal or select another application branch. Save the scenario and state seed with the capture.

Observe navigation, redirects, failed subresources, console output, and page exceptions. Do not inject repairs into the observation; test an intervention separately. Even a reasonable privacy choice, such as blocking analytics, changes the network policy and belongs in the record.
bullets: Pin browser family and exact version for comparable reruns.
Record viewport, locale, time zone, reduced-motion setting, and color preference.
Start from a named cookie and storage state.
Store failed requests and page exceptions with timestamps.
Mark every interception, mock, or blocked resource as an intervention.

sections.title: Define when this page is complete
paragraphs: Network idle is not a content test. Telemetry, chat, streams, and polling may never stop; a quiet network may still leave an empty page. Fixed sleeps can be too short under load or waste time after completion. Define observable conditions for the page type instead.

A product test might require a main heading, price, image state, canonical, product record, and no fatal application error. An article might require its title, body threshold, publication metadata, and internal navigation. Bound the test with a wall-clock deadline and label complete, partial, timed out, blocked, or failed outcomes.

Carry that label into extraction. Fields observed in a partial DOM remain evidence, but missing conditions stay uncertain. Dropping completeness can turn unfinished navigation into a false orphan-page finding or content-absence claim.

sections.title: Compare meaning before markup
paragraphs: String diffs are crowded by generated IDs, attribute order, hydration markers, timestamps, and framework wrappers. First compare source and DOM fields relevant to the claim: headings, visible text, links, canonical, robots directives, language alternates, structured records, forms, media, and named components.

Classify each field as added, removed, changed, or unchanged and point to both captures. Resolve links while retaining original hrefs and anchors. Compare parsed structured records by stable identity, not JSON key order. Report exact and normalized text so normalization cannot conceal a meaningful delta.

Use serialized DOM to investigate the component behind a field change. Starting with the operational difference keeps the report focused on what delivery or discovery changed, rather than every framework mutation.

codeExamples.title: Render envelope
codeExamples.description: The completeness result and artifact references travel with every extracted field.

sections.title: Find which stage failed
paragraphs: Source absent, DOM present: was client delivery intentional, and did the completion test pass? Source present, DOM absent: inspect component logic, hydration, consent, and runtime errors. Both present but reported missing: reproduce extraction on saved captures before changing the site.

Browser capability and crawler accessibility are separate. Google documents crawling, rendering, and indexing for JavaScript pages; local Chromium is not a Googlebot result. It can establish dependence on client execution in the tested scenario, not failure across every downstream system.

After repair, repeat the request headers, browser version, scenario, completion contract, and extractor. Verify the expected delta without new failure states. An environment change creates a new comparison; it cannot silently close the old finding.
